newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia's Kras continues EBRD talks, no deal yet.
newsitem.headline: Croatia's Kras continues EBRD talks, no deal yet.

text.p: Croatia's leading confectioner Kras d.d. said on Thursday it was still negotiating with the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) on investment and no deal of any kind was imminent.
"There is no new element (in the talks), we are still negotiating," finance director Tomislav Jovic told Reuters by telephone.

Rumours that the EBRD was close to buying into Kras and that the company would then list its shares abroad, like drugs firm Pliva did earlier this year, have pushed the price of its stock to a record 430 kuna on Wednesday on Zagreb's bourse.
A steep rise, totalling 115 kuna over the past 10 days with a series of all-time highs, was boosted by a solid 1995 profit report released last week.

But Jovic said talks with the EBRD may take a few months to complete. He added that for now they centred on a credit line of between 30 and 40 million German marks to modernise Kras's chocolate production.

The company annually invests some 11 million marks of its own resources into development. It exports some 25 percent of its total sales, which reached almost $80 million last year. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
